2  THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The insurer is in appeal challenging its liability to pay the compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT at Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC Nos.773/2015 and 940/2015, vide judgment and award dated 02.11.2017.
2.

The claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by the claimants in a road traffic accident on 19.04.2015, were entertained by the Tribunal and the following compensation was awarded:

In MVC No.773/2015:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Towards pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2. Towards medical expenses 6,592/-
 3. Towards future income 1,14,240/-
 4. Towards attendant's 29,000/-
 charges, food and  conveyance

5. Towards loss of amenities 10,000/-
 and nutrition food  6. Towards loss of income 21,000/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5519  during the period of  treatment  Total 2,10,832/-

In MVC No.940/2015:

3.

In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal rejected the contention of the insurer that the insurer is not liable to indemnify the owner on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess an endorsement to drive a transport vehicle.

The Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle did possess a valid licence to drive a light motor vehicle and therefore, fastened NC: 2023:KHC-K:5519 the liability to pay the compensation upon the insurer.
Being aggrieved by aforesaid finding regarding liability, the insurer is in appeals.

4. Learned counsel for the insurer contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence to drive the transport vehicle as he possessed a licence only to drive a light motor vehicle (non-transport).
He therefore, submitted that the insurer was exempted from the liability to indemnify the owner.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the issue is no longer res-integra in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs.
Oriental
Insurance Company Limited1.

6. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the issue regarding liability raised by the insurer in these appeals is squarely covered by the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of the Mukund Dewangan.

Consequently, the insurer cannot avoid its liability to pay the compensation (2017) 14 SCC 663 NC:
2023:KHC-K:5519 awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, these appeals lack merit and are dismissed.
7. Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
